svg.title: First line after metastasis: the licence changed, the reimbursement did not
svg.desc: Schematic in two stacked layers with a broken arrow between them. The figure is stamped with the verification date 2026-09-13; every licence and reimbursement clause stops on that date. The top layer, "guidelines and the marketing licence: changed", holds three cards. The first is EV-302 / KEYNOTE-A39, first line, randomised phase III, global and open label, in 886 patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab 442, chemotherapy 444). The registration analysis, median follow-up 17.2 months, gave median overall survival 31.5 vs 16.1 months, hazard ratio 0.47 (0.38 to 0.58); the 2.5-year update gave 33.8 months (95% confidence interval 26.1 to 39.3) vs 15.9 (13.6 to 18.3), hazard ratio 0.51 (0.43 to 0.61), and median progression-free survival 12.5 vs 6.3 months, hazard ratio 0.48 (0.41 to 0.57). Both sets are correct but must not be mixed; with longer follow-up the medians rise and so does the hazard ratio. The same card carries the response rates: confirmed objective response 67.7% (63.1 to 72.1) vs 44.4% (39.7 to 49.2) in the 437 and 441 patients with measurable disease at baseline, and complete response 29.1% vs 12.5%, with the warning that a response rate is not a cure rate, that a complete response is not a cure because the median overall survival of the whole population is still 33.8 months, and that of the 373 patients with a recorded outcome peripheral neuropathy resolved completely in 13% while 87% still had residual neuropathy at the last assessment. The second card holds the two roads with randomised evidence for those who cannot have that combination: JAVELIN Bladder 100, 700 patients without progression after four to six cycles of platinum chemotherapy, one-year survival 71.3% vs 58.4%, median overall survival 21.4 vs 14.3 months, hazard ratio 0.69 (0.56 to 0.86), grade 3 or above adverse events 47.4% vs 25.2%, with the list of who it does not apply to; and CheckMate 901, 608 patients fit for cisplatin, median follow-up 33.6 months, median overall survival 21.7 vs 18.9 months, hazard ratio 0.78 (0.63 to 0.96), P=0.02, complete response 21.7% vs 11.8%, median duration of complete response 37.1 vs 13.2 months, grade 3 or above adverse events 61.8% vs 51.7%, and only 9% of the control arm on avelumab maintenance. The third card is the Taiwanese licence: TFDA licence number 001212 for enfortumab vedotin, amended 2026-05-08, now registered for use in combination with pembrolizumab in adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma. A licence is permission to sell, not a decision to pay. The broken arrow between the layers reads "the licence exists; the reimbursement does not". The bottom layer, "Taiwan National Health Insurance: unchanged", holds three cards. The first is clause 9.109 for enfortumab vedotin, in force from 1 May 2024, labelled third line, monotherapy and six cycles per lifetime, with the clause quoted verbatim and the lifetime ceiling of 6 cycles; the evidence behind it is EV-301, 608 patients, median overall survival 12.88 vs 8.97 months, hazard ratio 0.70 (0.56 to 0.89). The second is clause 9.69 and the two cells that are paid for: nivolumab with cisplatin and gemcitabine for up to 6 cycles followed by nivolumab alone as first-line treatment, requiring a glomerular filtration rate of 60 or above; and avelumab maintenance after 4 to 6 cycles without progression in partial response or stable disease, noting that JAVELIN Bladder 100 enrolled patients without progression, which includes a complete response. The third card is drawn as an empty dashed box containing only the words "zero hits": a full-text search of the regulations for first-line enfortumab vedotin with pembrolizumab returns nothing, which means no entry was found rather than "not reimbursed" or "so you must pay yourself" - ask the medical affairs office. No price appears anywhere. The closing band states that this page stops on 2026-09-13, should not be used as today's rule, and must not be used to stop or change any treatment.

g.text: METASTATIC UROTHELIAL CARCINOMA - THE
GUIDELINE AND THE LICENCE CHANGED, THE
REIMBURSEMENT DID NOT
First line after
metastasis: the top layer
changed, the bottom layer
did not
The top layer is the international guideline and the
Taiwanese marketing licence; the bottom layer is
Taiwan's National Health Insurance. The broken
arrow between them carries the whole weight of this
article: the licence exists, the reimbursement does
not.
Every figure carries its trial name, line of therapy,
population, n, endpoint and follow-up. One rule holds
throughout: a response rate is not a cure rate.
Verified 2026-09-13
Every licence and every reimbursement clause here stops on this
date, and the trial figures run only to what had been published by
then. Ask what the position is today.
Top layer
Guidelines and the marketing licence:
changed
The international guideline changed the combination, and so did the
Taiwanese licence.
EV-302 / KEYNOTE-A39
First line
Randomised phase III
Global, open label
Previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic
urothelial carcinoma, 886 patients (enfortumab vedotin plus
pembrolizumab 442 / chemotherapy 444); the chemotherapy
arm received gemcitabine with cisplatin or carboplatin
according to cisplatin eligibility.
Registration analysis (median follow-up 17.2 months)
Median overall survival 31.5 vs 16.1 months, hazard ratio
2.5-year median follow-up update
Median overall survival 33.8 months (95% confidence
interval 26.1 to 39.3) vs 15.9 (13.6 to 18.3), hazard ratio 0.51
(0.43 to 0.61); median progression-free survival 12.5 vs 6.3
months, hazard ratio 0.48 (0.41 to 0.57)
Both sets are correct, but they must not be mixed; say which
analysis is being quoted. With longer follow-up the medians
rise and so does the hazard ratio (0.47 becomes 0.51), which
is how long follow-up normally behaves.
A hazard ratio divides the rate at which events occur in one
arm by the rate in the other; 0.51 means deaths occurred at
roughly half the rate of the control arm, not that anyone lived
twice as long.
Confirmed objective response rate and complete
response rate
with measurable disease at baseline (437 vs 441)
Complete response 29.1% vs 12.5%
A response rate is not a cure rate. A complete response
is not a cure - it means the tumour can no longer be
measured on imaging, while the median overall survival
of the whole trial population is still 33.8 months.
The next figure in the same label belongs beside it: of the
373 patients with a recorded outcome, peripheral
neuropathy resolved completely in 13%, and 87% still had
residual neuropathy at the last assessment.
For those who cannot have that combination:
two roads with randomised evidence
Both randomised phase III
The two trials enrolled different people, and the labels cannot
be dropped.
JAVELIN Bladder 100: avelumab maintenance after
platinum chemotherapy
700 patients who had had four to six cycles of first-line
gemcitabine with cisplatin or carboplatin without
progression: one-year survival 71.3% vs 58.4%, median
overall survival 21.4 vs 14.3 months, hazard ratio 0.69
(0.56 to 0.86); grade 3 or above adverse events 47.4% vs
CheckMate 901: nivolumab added for those fit for cisplatin
608 patients, median follow-up 33.6 months, median overall
survival 21.7 vs 18.9 months, hazard ratio 0.78 (0.63 to
0.96), P=0.02; complete response 21.7% vs 11.8%, median
duration of complete response 37.1 vs 13.2 months; grade 3
or above adverse events 61.8% vs 51.7%
Who JAVELIN does not apply to belongs in the same
paragraph: anyone who progressed during chemotherapy,
anyone who did not complete four to six cycles, and anyone
given enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab in the first line.
CheckMate 901 enrolled only patients fit for cisplatin, and only
9% of its control arm received avelumab maintenance - which
makes the comparison with "chemotherapy then
maintenance" an unequal one.
The Taiwanese marketing licence (TFDA)
Licence: yes
TFDA licence 衛部菌疫輸字第001212號 (enfortumab vedotin),
The registered indication now carries this clause
(verbatim)
"In combination with pembrolizumab for the treatment of
adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial
carcinoma (mUC)"
A marketing licence is permission to sell. It is not a decision
to pay. The layer below is where payment is decided.
The licence exists; the reimbursement
does not
This article is not titled "the first line has changed"
because of exactly this gap. On the guideline and on the
licence it is true; on the reimbursement it is not.
Bottom layer
Taiwan National Health Insurance:
unchanged
The clauses are quoted verbatim, and nothing is inferred from
them.
Clause 9.109, enfortumab vedotin (in force from
Third line
Monotherapy
Six cycles per lifetime
"For adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic
urothelial carcinoma who have previously received
platinum-containing chemotherapy and whose disease has
progressed after failure of a subsequent immune
checkpoint inhibitor (such as atezolizumab, nivolumab,
pembrolizumab, avelumab or ipilimumab)"
"Each patient is reimbursed for a maximum of 6 cycles"
That is a lifetime ceiling, not a recommended number of
cycles.
Which trial this cell corresponds to
EV-301: 608 patients who had had platinum AND progressed
during or after a PD-1 / PD-L1 inhibitor; median overall
survival 12.88 vs 8.97 months, hazard ratio 0.70 (0.56 to 0.89).
Clause 9.69: the two cells that are paid for
First line with chemotherapy
Maintenance
"Nivolumab is limited to combination with cisplatin and
gemcitabine for up to 6 cycles, followed by nivolumab
alone, as first-line treatment for adult patients with
unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma"
It also requires a glomerular filtration rate of 60 or above.
Avelumab maintenance reads "after 4 to 6 cycles, without
disease progression, and having achieved a partial
response (PR) or stable disease (SD)"
Where the clause and the trial differ, both are set down as
written
JAVELIN Bladder 100 enrolled patients "without
progression", which includes a complete response; the
clause says PR or SD. No interpretation is offered here.
First-line enfortumab vedotin with
pembrolizumab
Full-text search
Zero hits
What zero hits means
No entry was found. It does not mean "definitely not
reimbursed", and it does not mean "so you must pay for it
yourself" - ask the medical affairs office how to apply. No
price of any kind appears on this figure, because no official
announcement could be found to quote.
How long this page is good for
Every licence and every reimbursement clause above stops on
2026-09-13, and the trial figures run only to what had been published
by then.
Ask what the position is today rather than treating this as the current
rule, and do not stop or change any treatment on the strength of it.
Schematic, redrawn from the EV-302/KEYNOTE-A39 registration and
2.5-year analyses, the FDA prescribing information for enfortumab
vedotin, JAVELIN Bladder 100, CheckMate 901, EV-301, the EAU
Guidelines on Muscle-invasive and Metastatic Bladder Cancer (2026), the
Taiwan National Health Insurance Drug Benefit Regulations and the TFDA
dataset of current drug licences; not reproduced from any published
figure. Populations, designs and endpoints differ between studies, so the
points are not directly comparable.
